title: A nonzero polynomial relation lowers the dimension of a quasi-finite polynomial algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $n\ge0$ be an integer, and let $T$ be a commutative finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\varphi:k[t_1,\dots,t_n]\to T$ be a $k$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] which is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. If $\ker\varphi$ contains a nonzero polynomial, then $\dim\operatorname{Spec}T<n$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The zero ring is permitted, with empty spectrum of dimension $-\infty$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), proof, last sentence: the nonzero residue-polynomial kernel implies the strict dimension bound; a general field-algebra input behind that inference.
